title: Age, surface variation and ground contact for the Prairie Avenue 1904 programme (package K14, the kit)
status: Declared and evaluated, not yet built to. No structure in the scene takes its condition from this kit today; T-2325 applies it to a named Prairie Avenue house and its yard. The K03 1808 service wall (T-2291) keeps its own damp and soot constants until then, and they are this kit's full-age values (the check holds the two equal).
rule: Condition is a LAYER over a clean fabric, never baked into a fabric map, and it is the condition of each building ON 1904-07-01: the darkening a maintained house of its own age had gathered, not the state of a neglected one. Every layer is a function of position on a surface (metres above grade, metres below the soffit, metres from a source, metres from a wall foot or a path's centre line), of the building's years standing at the target date, of the fabric it lies on and of the property's own seed, and returns a multiplier in [floor, 1] (wall layers, for the renderer's _TONE vertex channel or a baked mask) or a weight in [0, 1] (ground layers, the share of bare earth or worn surface). Layers multiply; the product is held at the floor. Nothing here removes, moves or adds fabric: no layer may express any condition in `never`. Every number is reconstructed, from the study's sparse-evidence rules and the two masks already shipped, and is recorded as L-k14-condition-kit-2324.

floor.note: The darkest any point of a 1904 wall may read, as a multiplier on its clean fabric: the eave soot and the ground damp of a 40-year-old wall, both at full strength on the most absorbent stone, would cross it. Below it a wall stops reading as its material (a pale limestone front turns charcoal), which is the 'modern ruin' T-1856 rules out.

age.note: a = clamp(years / full_years, 0, 1), years counted from the building's completion to target_date. Prairie Avenue's oldest standing houses in 1904 date from the late 1860s and early 1870s, so 40 years is the oldest wall the district has; a layer reaches its full-age value there and grows no further. A house of 1900 to 1904 (new Georgian Revival work) is a = 0 to 0.1 and reads clean.

seed.rule: seed = first 8 hex digits of sha256('k14|' + structure_id), as an integer. Every stochastic choice (a band edge's wobble, a trail's length, a lawn edge's line, a repaint year) draws from it, so a property's condition is the same on every build and independent of its neighbours'.
seed.note: Keyed to the stable structure id the per-building tickets keep, so a refinement keeps its weathering.

ground_damp._doc: Rising damp and rain splash at a wall foot: a band darkest at grade, fading to the clean body at its top. Its top wobbles along the wall by the property's seed.
ground_damp.note: full-age top and tone are the K03 1808 service wall's (T-2291, L-k03-1808-service-brick-2291): a splash zone up to the height rain throws off a hard yard.

eave_soot._doc: The sheltered band under an eave that rain does not wash: darkest at the soffit, clean at its lower edge.
eave_soot.note: full-age depth and tone are the K03 1808 service wall's (T-2291): soot settles where the wall is never rinsed, which is under the eave.

water_trails._doc: A streak below each source, as wide as its source at the top and narrowing by `taper` at its foot, darkest under the source and clean at its length, broken across its width into rivulets (strength 1 - streaks to 1, about one per streak_wavelength_m). Its length draws from the seed within +/- jitter.
water_trails.note: A sill throws its run-off over its ends and front; an overflow spout or a hopper head that spills leaves a longer, darker streak. Lengths are set so a sill's trail never reaches the head of the window below on a 3.5 m storey.

chimney_soot._doc: A plume on the covering leeward of a stack: within half_angle_deg of the lee bearing, darkest at the stack and clean at length_m. The stack's own sooted band is K15's (k15_chimneys.json soot).
chimney_soot.note: Chicago's prevailing winds are westerly to south-westerly, so smoke lays down to the east-north-east; bearing 70 degrees, clockwise from north. A slate or tin roof is relaid and painted less often than a wall is cleaned, so the plume keeps its full strength.

mortar._doc: Mortar joints built as geometry darken and recess further with age. A fabric-map joint (an LOD panel) takes only the tone.
mortar.note: A soft lime joint erodes and collects dirt; a dense tinted joint of a pressed front barely moves. Ids are the K03 library's mortars (assets/textures/prairie_1904_brick/profiles.json).

paint._doc: Painted joinery and cladding weather only since their last repaint: paint age = (years + seed mod cycle) mod cycle, never more than years. The tone is dulling dirt; the paint never fails to bare wood.
paint.note: A kept house of 1904 repainted its exterior woodwork every five to seven years, so a 38-year-old frame house's paint is never older than its cycle. The seed spreads the repaint years so a street of frame houses does not weather in step.

grass_edge._doc: A bare strip at a wall foot where a lawn meets the wall (drip line, splash and shade): weight 1 at the wall, 0 past width, with the line wobbling by the seed.
grass_edge.note: Kept lawns, cut to an edge by a gardener; the strip is narrow and never widens into a dirt yard. A newly sodded front has almost none.

path_wear._doc: Wear across a walk or drive by its use: a walk wears along its centre, a drive in two wheel tracks. Weight 1 on the worn line, 0 at core_half_m + falloff_m from it; scaled by the age factor and the use's strength.
path_wear.note: A front walk of stone flags is swept and shows a polish, a cinder or gravel service walk a beaten line, a carriage drive two tracks at about a carriage's 1.5 m gauge.

fabric_response._doc: How strongly each fabric shows a wall layer: the layer's darkening (1 - tone) is multiplied by this before the floor is applied. Ids are the K02 stone and K03 brick libraries'.
fabric_response.note: Pale porous stone shows soot most and a dense dark pressed brick or granite least; the multipliers are relative and keep every fabric's own colour, since the layer is a grey multiplier and never a tint.

never: vegetation growing on a wall or roof
a black or uniformly grimed facade
a condition darker than the floor
